Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: Bitar and Aflak slowly gained supporters and in 1945 the first elected Bureau of the Arab Ba'ath Movement was formed, including both men.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: The organisation gained many new members when most of the former supporters of Al-_____, led by Wahib al-Ghanim, joined it
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: Al-Arsuzi set up his own Arab Ba'ath party in 1940 and he disagreed with Bitar and Aflak on the Iraqi coup, arguing it was doomed to fail, while the two men were enthusiastic and wanted to send volunteers to Iraq. Al-Arsuzi's movement faded away following his exile by the French.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: According to _____, "Aflak and Arsuzi's achievement was to help lift this burden of guilt and inferiority
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: According to Patrick Seale, "Aflak and Arsuzi's achievement was to help lift this burden of guilt and inferiority.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: Aflak formulated a theory and a programme to rouse the _____ from what he considered a living death
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: According to Bitar, most of the students joined them and not the communist party as "any political movement in Syria cannot materialize except through Arab nationalism", indicating that national independence was the priority at the time, rather than social issues. Aflak formulated a theory and a programme to rouse the Arab from what he considered a living death.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: In _____ Syria's military leader Adib al-Shishakli banned all political parties
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: In 1952 Syria's military leader Adib al-Shishakli banned all political parties.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: The three politicians agreed to merge their parties and co-operated in the overthrow of Shishakli in _____, following which a congress ratified the merger of the two parties into the Arab Socialist Ba
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: The three politicians agreed to merge their parties and co-operated in the overthrow of Shishakli in 1954, following which a congress ratified the merger of the two parties into the Arab Socialist Ba'ath Party.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: The rules and constitution of _____ and Aflaq's party were adopted unchanged
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: Bitar and Aflaq took refuge in neighboring Lebanon, where they came into contact with Akram al-Hawrani—an experienced politician who had recently set up the Arab Socialist Party and had a considerable following among the peasantry of the Hama region in central Syria and a valuable foothold in the military officer corps. The rules and constitution of Bitar and Aflaq's party were adopted unchanged.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: All three were elected to the party's new _____, along with a supporter of Hawrani
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: All three were elected to the party's new National Command, along with a supporter of Hawrani.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: Bitar was elected as a deputy for Damascus, defeating the secretary general of the _____—one of the Ba'ath's bitterest ideological enemies
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: Bitar was elected as a deputy for Damascus, defeating the secretary general of the Syrian Social National Party—one of the Ba'ath's bitterest ideological enemies.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: He became Minister for Foreign Affairs in _____ and held the post until 1958
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: He became Minister for Foreign Affairs in 1956 and held the post until 1958.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: Along with other Ba'athists, he agitated in favour of the unification of Syria with _____'s Egypt
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: Along with other Ba'athists, he agitated in favour of the unification of Syria with Nasser's Egypt. He and other Syrians in the UAR leadership became dismayed over the dominant role Nasser gave the Egyptians in administrating the UAR.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: At the beginning, Bitar was the only _____ in the central cabinet
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: Bitar was elected as a deputy for Damascus, defeating the secretary general of the Syrian Social National Party—one of the Ba'ath's bitterest ideological enemies. At the beginning, Bitar was the only Syrian in the central cabinet.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: He and other _____ in the UAR leadership became dismayed over the dominant role Nasser gave the Egyptians in administrating the UAR
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: He and other Syrians in the UAR leadership became dismayed over the dominant role Nasser gave the Egyptians in administrating the UAR. Nasser had opposed the formation of a joint leadership council of Egyptians and Syrians.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: Nasser had opposed the formation of a joint leadership council of _____ and Syrians
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: He and other Syrians in the UAR leadership became dismayed over the dominant role Nasser gave the Egyptians in administrating the UAR. Nasser had opposed the formation of a joint leadership council of Egyptians and Syrians.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: The resignation were made public, and were accepted later in _____
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: On 23–24 December 1959 Bitar—together with Hawrani (the UAR Vice President and central Minister of Justice), Mustafa Hamdun (Syrian regional Minister of Agriculture and Agrarian Reform) and Abd al-Ghani Qannut (the Syrian regional social affairs and labour minister), as well as all former members of the Syrian Regional Branch of the Ba'ath Party who worked within the UAR bureaucracy—resigned their posts. The resignation were made public, and were accepted later in December.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: A fifth Syrian regional minister, Khalil al-Khallas, the Minister of Economy and a member of the Executive Council of Syria (the Syrian regional government), resigned in January _____
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: A fifth Syrian regional minister, Khalil al-Khallas, the Minister of Economy and a member of the Executive Council of Syria (the Syrian regional government), resigned in January 1960. Syrians began to resign en masse, and by August 1960 only three Syrians remained in the official decision-making bodies of the UAR.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: Syrians began to resign en masse, and by August _____ only three Syrians remained in the official decision-making bodies of the UAR
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: A fifth Syrian regional minister, Khalil al-Khallas, the Minister of Economy and a member of the Executive Council of Syria (the Syrian regional government), resigned in January 1960. Syrians began to resign en masse, and by August 1960 only three Syrians remained in the official decision-making bodies of the UAR.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: The lack of Syrian participation was "corrected" in September when five new Syrian cabinet members were appointed, but the ratio of two Egyptians for each Syrian central cabinet member was kept until
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: The lack of Syrian participation was "corrected" in September when five new Syrian cabinet members were appointed, but the ratio of two Egyptians for each Syrian central cabinet member was kept until 1961. Bitar supported the coup of 28 September 1961, which dissolved the UAR as a de facto union between Egypt and Syria.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: Bitar supported the coup of 28 September _____, which dissolved the UAR as a de facto union between Egypt and Syria
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: The lack of Syrian participation was "corrected" in September when five new Syrian cabinet members were appointed, but the ratio of two Egyptians for each Syrian central cabinet member was kept until 1961. Bitar supported the coup of 28 September 1961, which dissolved the UAR as a de facto union between Egypt and Syria.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: On 2 October _____, Bitar, Hawrani and 14 other politicians—mostly conservatives—signed a manifesto
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: The lack of Syrian participation was "corrected" in September when five new Syrian cabinet members were appointed, but the ratio of two Egyptians for each Syrian central cabinet member was kept until 1961. Bitar supported the coup of 28 September 1961, which dissolved the UAR as a de facto union between Egypt and Syria.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: From December _____, Bitar and the Ba'ath Party began to oppose the UAR and its political structure
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: From December 1959, Bitar and the Ba'ath Party began to oppose the UAR and its political structure.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: Two months later, Bitar signed a similar document, the _____ for the Separatist Regime
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: Two months later, Bitar signed a similar document, the National Charter for the Separatist Regime.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: His signing both of these documents was used against him in the _____ Unity Talks between Egypt, Iraq and Syria as proof of him lacking pro-Arab nationalist credentials
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: His signing both of these documents was used against him in the 1963 Unity Talks between Egypt, Iraq and Syria as proof of him lacking pro-Arab nationalist credentials.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: The manifesto, which was handwritten by Bitar, stated that _____ had distorted "the idea of Arab nationalism" and accused him of strangling the "political and democratic life" in Syria
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: The manifesto, which was handwritten by Bitar, stated that Nasser had distorted "the idea of Arab nationalism" and accused him of strangling the "political and democratic life" in Syria.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: Bitar, then under popular criticism, withdrew his signature from the 2 _____ manifesto, but it was too late to prevent damage
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: Bitar, then under popular criticism, withdrew his signature from the 2 October manifesto, but it was too late to prevent damage.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: Several members called upon _____ to expel Bitar from the party, citing his wild opportunism
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: Several members called upon Aflaq to expel Bitar from the party, citing his wild opportunism. Because of this, Aflaq became the unquestionable leader of the Ba'ath Party.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: Because of this, _____ became the unquestionable leader of the Ba'ath Party
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: Several members called upon Aflaq to expel Bitar from the party, citing his wild opportunism. Because of this, Aflaq became the unquestionable leader of the Ba'ath Party.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: After the dissolution of the UAR, Bitar did not join the reconstituted Syrian Regional Branch of the Ba'ath Party until after the 8 March _____ Syrian coup d'état
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: After the dissolution of the UAR, Bitar did not join the reconstituted Syrian Regional Branch of the Ba'ath Party until after the 8 March 1963 Syrian coup d'état.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: All vital ministries except the defense ministry—which was headed by independent _____ al-Sufi—were given to Ba'athists
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: All vital ministries except the defense ministry—which was headed by independent Nasserite General Muhammad al-Sufi—were given to Ba'athists.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: The Ba'athist–_____ coalition government was unstable and based upon power politics rather than any sort of allegiance
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: All vital ministries except the defense ministry—which was headed by independent Nasserite General Muhammad al-Sufi—were given to Ba'athists. The Ba'athist–Nasserite coalition government was unstable and based upon power politics rather than any sort of allegiance.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: Many members wanted to turn the Ba'ath into a Syria-focused party and did not care about _____'s position towards Syria
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: All vital ministries except the defense ministry—which was headed by independent Nasserite General Muhammad al-Sufi—were given to Ba'athists. The Ba'athist–Nasserite coalition government was unstable and based upon power politics rather than any sort of allegiance.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: Bitar and Aflaq sought to gain popular legitimacy among the _____ people and viewed the coalition government as a means towards gaining the blessings of Nasser, who was still popular in Syria
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: Bitar and Aflaq sought to gain popular legitimacy among the Syrian people and viewed the coalition government as a means towards gaining the blessings of Nasser, who was still popular in Syria.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: This faction later became known as the "_____" ("Qutriyyin")
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: This faction later became called the "Regionalists" ("Qutriyyin").

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: He represented Syria at the Egyptian–Syrian–Iraqi unity negotiations of March–April _____
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: He represented Syria at the Egyptian–Syrian–Iraqi unity negotiations of March–April 1963.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: In the first round of negotiations, which lasted until 19 March when Bitar and Aflaq joined in, the Ba'ath Party was represented by Abd al-_____—the economy minister
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: In the first round of negotiations, which lasted until 19 March when Bitar and Aflaq joined in, the Ba'ath Party was represented by Abd al-Karim Zuhur—the economy minister.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: Nasser treated them badly during the negotiations, and Bitar and Aflaq moved closer to the position of the _____
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: Nasser treated them badly during the negotiations, and Bitar and Aflaq moved closer to the position of the Regionalists.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: Nasser would only resume negotiations if the Ba'ath Party made concessions to the _____ in Syria, which the Ba'athists refused to do
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: Nasser would only resume negotiations if the Ba'ath Party made concessions to the Nasserites in Syria, which the Ba'athists refused to do. Bitar and Lu'ay al-Atassi, the NCRC chairman, sharply rebuked the Nasserites.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: Propaganda campaigns by both Ba'athist and _____ forces ensued in Syria
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: Nasser would only resume negotiations if the Ba'ath Party made concessions to the Nasserites in Syria, which the Ba'athists refused to do. The Nasserite cabinet members of the United Arab Front, Nihad al-Qasim, the deputy prime minister and justice minister, and Abd al-Wahhab Hawmad, the finance minister, resigned in protest because of the Ba'ath Party's position on the issue.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: Bitar and Lu'ay al-_____, the NCRC chairman, sharply rebuked the Nasserites
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: Bitar and Lu'ay al-Atassi, the NCRC chairman, sharply rebuked the Nasserites.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: After the signing of the _____ of 17 April, the Nasserites demanding more power for themselves in the political system
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: After the signing of the Federal Union Agreement of 17 April, the Nasserites demanding more power for themselves in the political system.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: Both parties were averse to power-sharing but the _____ were outmaneuvered following the purge of their supporters in the officer corps, which ended their struggle for control over Syria
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: Bitar and Lu'ay al-Atassi, the NCRC chairman, sharply rebuked the Nasserites. After the signing of the Federal Union Agreement of 17 April, the Nasserites demanding more power for themselves in the political system.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: The Military Committee was adamantly opposed to continued negotiations with Nasser and the _____, and by the time of the purge, Aflaq and Bitar had given up on them
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: After the signing of the Federal Union Agreement of 17 April, the Nasserites demanding more power for themselves in the political system. Both parties were averse to power-sharing but the Nasserites were outmaneuvered following the purge of their supporters in the officer corps, which ended their struggle for control over Syria.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: After the negotiations with _____ ended, the Syrian government tried to maintain the illusion that they were continuing
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: After the signing of the Federal Union Agreement of 17 April, the Nasserites demanding more power for themselves in the political system. Both parties were averse to power-sharing but the Nasserites were outmaneuvered following the purge of their supporters in the officer corps, which ended their struggle for control over Syria.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: On 2 May, Bitar's government issued a decree calling for the nationalization of all _____ banks
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: After the negotiations with Nasser ended, the Syrian government tried to maintain the illusion that they were continuing. On 2 May, Bitar's government issued a decree calling for the nationalization of all Syrian banks.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: According to historian _____, this was probably not the first step to establish a state-owned economy
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: According to historian Itamar Rabinovich, this was probably not the first step to establish a state-owned economy.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: The purge of pro-_____ officers led the Nasserite cabinet members who had resigned on 25 March, to publicly tender their resignations for a second time on 6 May
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: Rabinovich said that this move was intended to deceive the Egyptians and the Nasserites; Nasser had previously told Bitar that the first step to revolutionary change was the nationalization of the banking sector. The purge of pro-Egyptian officers led the Nasserite cabinet members who had resigned on 25 March, to publicly tender their resignations for a second time on 6 May.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: Not long after, a violent demonstration occurred in _____
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: Not long after, a violent demonstration occurred in Damascus.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: It was violently put down by _____ al-Hafiz, the interior minister
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: It was violently put down by Amin al-Hafiz, the interior minister.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: The short-lived Ba'athist–_____ coalition government was dissolved on 11 May, and on 13 May, Bitar presented his second cabinet
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: The Nasserites said that they would withdraw their resignations if all of their demands were met. The short-lived Ba'athist–Nasserite coalition government was dissolved on 11 May, and on 13 May, Bitar presented his second cabinet.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: General Ghassan Haddad, an independent, took over Zuhur's post as planning minister and Ziad al-_____, the independent chief of staff, was appointed defense minister
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: General Ghassan Haddad, an independent, took over Zuhur's post as planning minister and Ziad al-Hariri, the independent chief of staff, was appointed defense minister. A power struggle between Hariri and the Military Committee occurred between 23 June and 8 July 1963.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: The formation of Bitar's second cabinet began a new phase in _____–Syrian relations; the Egyptian government stated that Bitar's cabinet was an "unjustified blow to the Union's state"
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: The formation of Bitar's second cabinet began a new phase in Egyptian–Syrian relations; the Egyptian government stated that Bitar's cabinet was an "unjustified blow to the Union's state". The Syrian media and press reported in kind, but their communiques made clear distinctions between Nasser and the "incompetent" people within the Egyptian government.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: The Syrian media and press reported in kind, but their communiques made clear distinctions between Nasser and the "incompetent" people within the _____ government
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: The formation of Bitar's second cabinet began a new phase in Egyptian–Syrian relations; the Egyptian government stated that Bitar's cabinet was an "unjustified blow to the Union's state". The Syrian media and press reported in kind, but their communiques made clear distinctions between Nasser and the "incompetent" people within the Egyptian government.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: A power struggle between Hariri and the Military Committee occurred between 23 June and 8 July _____
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: A power struggle between Hariri and the Military Committee occurred between 23 June and 8 July 1963.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: The Military Committee viewed _____'s independent power base with unease
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: A power struggle between Hariri and the Military Committee occurred between 23 June and 8 July 1963. The Military Committee viewed Hariri's independent power base with unease.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: Bitar supported _____ in his conflict against the Military Committee; presumably believing that Hariri worked as a check on the Military Committee's growing power
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: A power struggle between Hariri and the Military Committee occurred between 23 June and 8 July 1963. The Military Committee viewed Hariri's independent power base with unease.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: On the same day, a new Agrarian Reform Law—which abolished the _____ Agrarian Reform Law and amending the 1958 one—was published
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: On the same day, a new Agrarian Reform Law—which abolished the 1962 Agrarian Reform Law and amending the 1958 one—was published.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: Bitar had promised to introduce a new agrarian law for some time; according to _____ its publication was "probably fixed so as to serve the Ba'ath in its struggle against Hariri"
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: Bitar had promised to introduce a new agrarian law for some time; according to Rabinovich its publication was "probably fixed so as to serve the Ba'ath in its struggle against Hariri".

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: Hariri resisted the committee's move and promptly returned to _____ to marshal his supporters
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: Hariri resisted the committee's move and promptly returned to Damascus to marshal his supporters.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: Neither Hariri nor the _____ sought a violent confrontation, and when it became clear that the committee had a larger following in the officer corps, Hariri admitted defeat and left the country
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: Hariri resisted the committee's move and promptly returned to Damascus to marshal his supporters. Neither Hariri nor the Committee sought a violent confrontation, and when it became clear that the committee had a larger following in the officer corps, Hariri admitted defeat and left the country.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: He left for Paris on 8 July and was accompanied to the airport by _____ and Bitar
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: He left for Paris on 8 July and was accompanied to the airport by Haddad and Bitar.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: On 18 July, _____, a Nasserite officer, launched a coup against the Ba'athists
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: On 18 July, Jassem Alwan, a Nasserite officer, launched a coup against the Ba'athists.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: Alwan's attempted coup and _____'s demotion affected Egyptian–Syrian relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: President Atassi was removed from his post on 27 July and was replaced by Hafiz; according to Rabinovich, the Ba'athists thought it unnecessary to have an independent figurehead after the failed 18 July coup. Alwan's attempted coup and Atassi's demotion affected Egyptian–Syrian relations.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: On 22 July, the traditional date for Nasser's _____ address, Nasser stated that Egypt had withdrawn from the Federal Union Agreement, blaming the Ba'athists for the withdrawal
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: On 22 July, the traditional date for Nasser's Revolution Day address, Nasser stated that Egypt had withdrawn from the Federal Union Agreement, blaming the Ba'athists for the withdrawal.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: Once order had been restored after the coup attempt, Bitar dissolved his cabinet and appointed a new one on 4 _____
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: Once order had been restored after the coup attempt, Bitar dissolved his cabinet and appointed a new one on 4 August.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: Hafiz left the cabinet and was succeeded as interior minister by _____ al-Atassi
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: Hafiz left the cabinet and was succeeded as interior minister by Nureddin al-Atassi.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: However, things were not going according to _____'s and Aflaq's plan
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: Bitar's third cabinet was the first in which the Ba'athists controlled the government. However, things were not going according to Bitar's and Aflaq's plan.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: The reconstituted party was divided into many factions which differed on policy issues, but most of them supported Aflaq's ouster as _____ of the National Command
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: The reconstituted party was divided into many factions which differed on policy issues, but most of them supported Aflaq's ouster as Secretary General of the National Command.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: Immediately after the attempted coup, Aflaq and Bitar re-delegated basic organizational work to Hammud al-Shufi—the eventual Regional Secretary of the _____
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: Immediately after the attempted coup, Aflaq and Bitar re-delegated basic organizational work to Hammud al-Shufi—the eventual Regional Secretary of the Syrian Regional Branch.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: Shufi, who was at first believed to be an Aflaq supporter, was a radical _____
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: Shufi, who was at first believed to be an Aflaq supporter, was a radical Marxist.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: Shufi's group, which controlled the _____, became allies of the Military Committee in their fight to topple Aflaq and Bitar
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.fact: Shufi's group, which controlled the Syrian Regional Command, became allies of the Military Committee in their fight to topple Aflaq and Bitar.

Salah al-Din al-Bitar.subject: International Relations
Salah al-Din al-Bitar.question: Aflaq and Bitar could not rely upon support in the _____ from the Iraqis; the Iraqi Regional Branch had undergone a sudden radicalization under the leadership of Ali Salih al-Sa'di

Survey of Palestine.fact: The department grew significantly throughout the mandate period: it began with 46 professionals in 1921, of which 25 were recruited from outside Palestine, and by 1942 had 215 professionals, with only 11 recruited from outside Palestine. There were two schools for training Palestinian and Arab surveyors, one in Jenin that operated for one year starting 1942, and the other in Nazareth that opened in 1944.

Survey of Palestine.subject: International Relations
Survey of Palestine.question: However, during the _____ Arab–Israeli War, British lorries delivering the "Arab state" portion of their maps were diverted back to Tel Aviv
Survey of Palestine.fact: In early 1948, temporary Directors General of the Survey Department were appointed for each of the proposed "Jewish State" and "Arab State" under the terms of the United Nations Partition Plan for Palestine, and the pre-existing files and maps were to be shared. However, during the 1948 Arab–Israeli War, British lorries delivering the "Arab state" portion of their maps were diverted back to Tel Aviv.

Survey of Palestine.fact: Today, the historical maps are held at the Survey of Israel, the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development and Israeli Ministry of Defense archives.

Survey of Palestine.subject: International Relations
Survey of Palestine.question: This was followed by 1:5,000 provisional plans of _____ and its environs, which were reduced to 1:10,000 scale for general printing
Survey of Palestine.fact: Jerusalem 1:10,000 and 1:2,500 maps (see here): In 1936 a 1:2,500 map of the Old City of Jerusalem was published, the first detailed map since the 1865 Ordnance Survey of Jerusalem. This was followed by 1:5,000 provisional plans of Jerusalem and its environs, which were reduced to 1:10,000 scale for general printing.
